packageRules.description: kopf 1.39+ requires python>=3.10; ceph base image ships python3-cephfs only for system python 3.9. Unpin when ceph base bumps to a newer Stream.

Operators with upgrade/delete authority over cluster state: patch automerges, minor/major wait for a human (renovate-triage skill). rook-ceph sat 6 patches behind a CVE fix because this manager was off.

images/spilo-vchord base. Bumping it means re-checking that VectorChord is still inside the range Immich accepts, and that Spilo has not changed its shared_preload_libraries set. Only acid-immich uses this image.
oauth2-proxy gates every admin host; a bad bump locks everyone out (and it is what replaced authentik, 2026-09-23). Read the release notes, then merge by hand.

Upstream Gramps Web, now the FROM of images/grampsweb rather than the image the Deployment runs (hence the dockerfile manager). Pinned to `latest` by digest because upstream's version tags are months stale. :automergeDigest would otherwise merge a rebuild unseen, and a rebuild can move the bundled Gramps minor — desktop Gramps Web Sync only works when server and laptop agree on Gramps MAJOR.MINOR (60 today, laptop 6.0.6). Before merging, check the new image's GRAMPS_VERSION env (the workflow prints it and warns); if it is not 60, the laptop upgrades first or sync breaks. Merging this does NOT ship it: the workflow publishes a new sha- tag, and a second commit pins that tag in cluster/gramps/grampsweb.yaml. See docs/gramps.md.

Third-party MCP server with read access to the family tree, exposed publicly behind nothing but a bearer token. :automergeDigest would otherwise pull a new build unreviewed. Read the diff — particularly anything touching MCP_AUTH_TOKEN handling, MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS (DNS-rebinding protection) or the read-only tool split — before merging.

The MCP gateway is the OAuth front door for mcp.chrismiller.xyz AND holds an edge-ca client certificate that can create or delete OAuth clients in Dex, so a bad bump is an auth-plane incident. Never automerge: read the diff around the oauth/, proxy/ and webhook/ packages, and confirm telemetry is still opt-in per route.

Our own forward-auth validator (images/mcp-jwt-auth) — it IS the authorization decision for the MCP endpoint, so a bump is an auth change. The Deployment pins the sha- tag the workflow published; bump it deliberately after reading the diff, never automatically.

Our own Gramps Web (images/grampsweb): upstream plus the patch that creates a listed family address as an editor on first login. That patch decides who gets into the family tree with no human in the loop, so a bump is an auth change — read the diff and confirm the workflow's fail-closed smoke test passed. Renovate bumps the upstream FROM in the Dockerfile; the sha- tag here is pinned by hand after the workflow publishes it.
HA custom integrations/cards. A card bump must also move its ?v= resource in cluster/home-assistant/state/dashboards.yaml (hactl lint fails until it does); then hactl deploy + hactl apply.
HA core: read the breaking-changes section, pg_dumpall first, hactl lint in the new image (see docs/ha.md).
